newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Tan Chong plans restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Tan Chong plans restructuring.

text.p: Malaysian car assembler Tan Chong Motor Holdings Bhd said on Friday that it plans a restructuring which includes the spin-off of its autoparts, non-motor and foreign operations division to existing shareholders.
In a statement, it also said the motor division would be retained in Tan Chong.

The stock of Tan Chong, which assembles Nissan cars, was suspended on Friday pending a news announcement. Its stock closed at 4.76 ringgit on Thursday. Tan Chong requested a requotation in its shares from November 28.
Tan Chong said approved Bumiputera (ethnic Malay) investors would be invited to participate in the equity of the autoparts and non-motor divisions prior to the repayment of capital.

As part of the restructuring, Tan Chong said it would apply for the listing of the autoparts and non-motor divisions on the main board of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange and the foreign division on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong.

Tan Chong said its existing operations would be divided into four independent divisions comprising the local motor and truck assembly division or motor division, local autoparts manufacturing division, local non-motor division and foreign operations division.
Tan Chong said the disposal of the autoparts division will be for 567.45 million ringgit, while the non-motor division will be for 148.30 million ringgit.

The company said the restructuring was to enable each group to concentrate on its business and to enable existing shareholders of Tan Chong to participate directly in the equity interest of the divisions.
It is also seeking to comply with Malaysia's National Development Policy by increasing the Bumiputera content in Tan Chong autoparts and non-motor operations, it said.
After the restructuring, Tan Chong said its net tangible assets per share would rise to 1.87 ringgit from 77 cents.
The proposal is subject to various approvals including the Securities Commission, the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange and Tan Chong shareholders.
